strategies.title: Constrained triangular-lattice diameter minimization
strategies.plan: Start from the explicit 16-point triangular-lattice patch with row lengths \(3,5,5,3\), horizontal spacing 1, and vertical spacing \(\sqrt{3}/2\); it has \(d_{\min}=1\) and \(d_{\max}=\sqrt{13}\). Introduce an auxiliary variable \(z=D^2\), fix scale through the smooth inequalities \(\|p_i-p_j\|^2\ge1\), and minimize \(z\) subject to \(z-\|p_i-p_j\|^2\ge0\) for every pair, using deterministic SLSQP multistarts from the patch plus fixed sinusoidal perturbations rescaled to restore minimum separation 1. Supply analytic Jacobians: each separation constraint has gradients \(2(p_i-p_j)\) and \(-2(p_i-p_j)\), while each diameter constraint has their negatives and derivative 1 with respect to \(z\). Recompute the actual squared ratio after every solve and return only the best valid candidate, retaining the unmodified lattice patch as a fallback; this preserves exactly 16 finite 2D points and makes every accepted replacement a checkable strict improvement in the same min/max objective. The fallback alone has raw `min_max_ratio` \(1/13=0.0769230769>0.00153547329022\), and its converted `combined_score` is \((1/13)/(1/12.889266112)=0.991481...,` strictly exceeding the current ranking score 0.0197911238456.

strategies.title: Topology-diverse triangular shell search
strategies.plan: Use the existing hard formulation with auxiliary diameter-squared variable `z`, minimum-distance constraints `d_ij^2 >= 1`, and smooth linear objective `min z`, but replace the narrow perturbation-only start set by a deterministic portfolio of distinct triangular-row topologies. Include the incumbent `3-5-5-3` patch plus centered staggered unit triangular patches with row populations `4-4-4-4`, `4-5-4-3`, `3-4-5-4`, `5-6-5`, and `4-3-5-4`; normalize every start to exact minimum distance one before SLSQP. These starts alter the complete boundary-shell contact graph rather than merely changing coordinates within the incumbent basin, while the final full 16-point SLSQP remains free to remove the row structure. Preserve hard validity by retaining only finite candidates, centering and rescaling them, and accepting a candidate only when its directly recomputed squared ratio exceeds the incumbent value. The checkable gain condition is `ratio_squared(candidate) > ratio_squared(best)`, which implies `combined_score = ratio_squared(candidate)/(1/12.889266112) > 1.000003` for every accepted replacement; otherwise the valid incumbent fallback is returned, so the predicted combined_score is strictly greater than 1.000003 whenever a replacement is accepted.

strategies.title: Convex-hull seam replacement
strategies.plan: Starting from each optimized candidate, compute its convex hull deterministically with a monotone-chain hull routine, retain all non-hull points, and rebuild the hull subsystem as equally angle-spaced points around the retained-point centroid using the original hull cardinality. Set each new hull radius to the smallest radius for which every rebuilt-hull point is at least unit distance from every retained point and from its two hull neighbors, then use that rebuilt configuration as another hard-SLSQP start with the same auxiliary `z` constraints and analytic Jacobian. This is a mesoscopic replacement because it changes the entire diameter-bearing boundary while preserving the dense interior packing that establishes most minimum-distance contacts. Run the operation once from the incumbent and once from every topology-search winner, then compare actual pairwise ratios after normalization rather than trusting the solver status. The rebuild is always a valid finite 16-point configuration after its explicit distance scaling, and subsequent constraints preserve the normalized packing convention. The checkable gain condition is the same direct strict ratio comparison, so any accepted seam-repaired candidate has `combined_score > 1.000003`, with the original optimized configuration retained if no rebuilt hull improves it; the predicted combined_score is strictly greater than 1.000003 whenever a replacement is accepted.

strategies.title: Active-contact KKT polishing
strategies.plan: After obtaining the best hard-SLSQP candidate, identify all pairs within a relative tolerance of the minimum distance and all pairs within a relative tolerance of the diameter, for example `d_ij^2 <= 1+1e-7` and `d_ij^2 >= z-1e-7`. Remove translation and rotation null directions by fixing point zero at the origin and fixing the y-coordinate of the farthest point from point zero to zero after a deterministic rotation. Use the identified contacts as equality constraints in a least-squares KKT-style polish of the coordinates and `z`, then release back to the complete hard inequality problem so that omitted pairs can become active safely. This is local exploitation of the existing contact graph, unlike the topology and hull mechanisms, and is useful for recovering diameter reductions hidden by SLSQP termination tolerances and rigid-motion degeneracy. Accept only directly verified ratio improvements after restoring centering and minimum-distance normalization, so no equality-model approximation can degrade the returned result. The checkable gain condition is `ratio_squared(polished) > ratio_squared(best)`, hence every accepted polish has `combined_score > 1.000003` and otherwise the valid pre-polish candidate is returned; the predicted combined_score is strictly greater than 1.000003 whenever a replacement is accepted.

strategies.title: Gauge-fixed epigraph continuation
strategies.plan: Remove the three rigid-motion null directions before optimization: translate point 0 to the origin and rotate the configuration so the current long diagonal from point 0 to point 12 lies on the positive x-axis.  Optimize the smooth epigraph formulation with coordinates and a scalar \(z\), enforcing every pairwise constraint \(d_{ij}^2\ge1\) and \(d_{ij}^2\le z\), with analytic Jacobians, then exactly renormalize by the measured minimum distance and repeat from the result. Use deterministic sinusoidal coordinate modes plus the unperturbed compact seed, but retain only candidates whose directly recomputed squared ratio exceeds the currently retained candidate, so the incumbent is always a valid fallback. The gauge reduction improves SLSQP conditioning because translation and rotation otherwise create flat directions while \(z\) already converts the nonsmooth diameter objective into smooth inequality constraints. The acceptance test is a precise strict-improvement mechanism: any accepted candidate has `min_max_ratio > 0.0775841541474`, hence its predicted `combined_score = min_max_ratio / (1/12.889266112) > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Joint hull subsystem repair
strategies.plan: Starting from the best full solve, compute the convex hull with a deterministic monotone-chain routine and replace the entire hull coordinate subsystem at once while holding the non-hull points fixed. Solve the same all-pairs epigraph program over only hull coordinates and \(z\), then perform a complementary interior-only solve with the repaired hull fixed; repeat this hull/interior alternation a fixed small number of times. This is a mesoscopic replacement rather than a pointwise perturbation: diameter contacts are generally hull-to-hull, whereas the frozen interior preserves the dense minimum-distance contact network during the boundary repair. Every active solve retains both inequalities for all 120 pairs, including pairs with fixed endpoints, and the final result is accepted only after direct recomputation of the complete ratio. The acceptance test is a precise strict-improvement mechanism: any accepted candidate has `min_max_ratio > 0.0775841541474`, hence its predicted `combined_score = min_max_ratio / (1/12.889266112) > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Concentric-shell topology escape
strategies.plan: Add deterministic radial-shell seeds that do not inherit the incumbent’s row-contact topology: use shell populations `(1, 5, 10)`, `(3, 6, 7)`, `(4, 8, 4)`, and `(5, 6, 5)`, with each shell equally angularly spaced and successive shell radii separated by at least one. For a shell containing \(q\) points, choose its radius as the larger of the preceding radius plus one and \(1/(2\sin(\pi/q))\), so within-shell neighbor distances and between-shell radial lower bounds are at least one before refinement. Rotate each noncentral shell through fixed irrational-looking phases such as `0`, `0.271`, and `0.619`, normalize, and run the full analytic-Jacobian epigraph program from each shell construction. These starts are structurally distinct compact packings and can reach contact graphs inaccessible from a row-patch continuation, while all returned candidates are normalized and screened against every pairwise distance. The acceptance test is a precise strict-improvement mechanism: any accepted candidate has `min_max_ratio > 0.0775841541474`, hence its predicted `combined_score = min_max_ratio / (1/12.889266112) > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Contact-nullspace escape and epigraph release
strategies.plan: Retain the triangular-patch epigraph formulation, but after obtaining the best feasible configuration, identify all pairs within a relative tolerance of the current minimum distance and form their analytic squared-distance Jacobian. Project several deterministic sinusoidal displacement fields into the nullspace of those active minimum-contact gradients, normalize each displaced configuration back to minimum squared distance one, and rerun the full smooth epigraph SLSQP solve with analytic derivatives. This is a local active-set escape rather than another unconstrained perturbation: it preserves every tight separation to first order while allowing formerly inactive diameter pairs and boundary contacts to exchange roles. Keep the incumbent unless a candidate's directly recomputed `min(dsq)/max(dsq)` is larger, so failed escapes cannot reduce the returned score. The auxiliary variable remains \(z=d_{\max}^2\), with constraints \(d_{ij}^2\ge1\) and \(z-d_{ij}^2\ge0\), hence every release solve preserves the hard pairwise-distance formulation. The acceptance test is `ratio_squared(candidate) > 0.0775841541474`; because `combined_score = 12.889266112 * ratio_squared`, any accepted result has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Two-ring polar topology restart
strategies.plan: Add a structurally distinct deterministic family of starts consisting of eight outer and eight inner points on alternating regular octagons: outer angles \(2\pi k/8\), inner angles \(2\pi(k+1/2)/8\), with radius pairs \((R,r)=(2.70,2.00),(2.85,2.05),(3.00,2.15)\), followed by centering and normalization to minimum distance one. Also use the same three starts after applying the fixed anisotropic maps \(\operatorname{diag}(1.10,0.91)\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(0.91,1.10)\), then normalize again. Each start is released through the same analytic epigraph constraints, allowing the optimizer to replace the initially circular contact topology with a hull-and-interior topology that a triangular-lattice continuation may not reach. Reject all outputs except those with a directly measured ratio above the saved incumbent, so the polar construction is only an escape route and cannot damage validity or the incumbent result. The smooth auxiliary-variable constraints again enforce the exact min-distance/diameter problem rather than a soft surrogate. The acceptance test is `ratio_squared(candidate) > 0.0775841541474`; because `combined_score = 12.889266112 * ratio_squared`, any accepted result has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.
